en.title: Total Count of Good Subsequences Under Point Updates
en.description:
A non-empty subsequence is good if the GCD of all its elements is greater than 1. Perform the point replacements one by one; after each one, take the number of good subsequences modulo 10⁹+7, and finally add these reduced counts together directly. The final sum is not taken modulo. Choices of different indices are counted separately.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, solution, and tests.
en.input: The first line contains N Q (1..100000), and the second line contains N values of A (1..100000); then Q lines X Y follow, with 1≤X≤N and 1≤Y≤100000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation:
Example 1: the array becomes 2, 2; both single elements and the pair are valid, for 3 in total.

Example 2: after the two replacements there are 4 and 7 good subsequences respectively, for a sum of 11.

Example 3: the two replacements leave 4 copies of 2 and 3 copies of 2, giving 15 and 7 respectively, for a sum of 22.
hints: Use inclusion–exclusion over prime factors: each square-free factor d>1 contributes −μ(d)(2^count[d]−1). An update only changes the counts of these factors for the old value and the new value. Precompute the smallest prime factors and the powers of 2.
